fable.w: This section only defines terms used in the Act, such as administrative cost, Agency and major disaster. The tempting reading is that mentions of grantees, subgrantees and grant programs imply outside-party involvement, but these are definitional references and grant applications are not participation in any case. Nothing here sets up a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority or right to sue.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of definitions for terms used within the Act. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties. It merely defines internal agency costs, officials, and grant programs.
qwen_block.s: In this Act— (1) the term “administrative cost”... (2) the term “Administrator”... (3) the term “Agency”... (4) the term “direct administrative cost”... (5) the term “hazard mitigation program”... (6) the term “individual assistance program”... (7) the term “major disaster”... (8) the term “mission assignment”... (9) the term “public assistance program”...

opus.w: This section only defines terms such as 'administrative cost,' 'Agency,' and various FEMA grant programs. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. Grantees and subgrantees appear only as recipients of grants, and receiving benefits or grants is expressly excluded from participation.
opus.s: the term “public assistance program” means the public assistance grant program authorized under sections 403(a)(3), 406, 418, 419, 428, and 502(a) of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act
opus.b: This is a definitions section, so it does not require participation. The tempting reading is that because it mentions grantees, subgrantees and FEMA's individual and public assistance grant programs, it brings outside parties into federal decisions. That fails on two counts. The section only defines terms, and the definition expressly excludes applications for benefits or grants.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of definitions for terms used in the Act. It does not describe any process where the federal government consults with or coordinates with outside parties before making a decision. Defining who a grantee is does not constitute participation in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s:
In this Act—
    (1) the term “administrative cost”—
        (A) means a cost incurred by the Agency in support of the delivery of disaster assistance for a major disaster; and 
        (B) does not include a cost incurred by a grantee or subgrantee;
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that defining terms like "grantee" or "subgrantee" implies participation because these entities are outside the federal government. However, definitions alone do not establish a process of consultation, coordination, or public input into a federal decision. They merely define the scope of the statute.
